en: The Permanent Danger Zone around Mayon Volcano keeps people safe from sudden lava flows and deadly pyroclastic density currents.
Coastal residents in Tacloban City use elevated evacuation centers to stay safe from deadly storm surges during strong typhoons.
Swimming in the Cagayan River during the rainy season is dangerous because sudden flash floods can occur without warning.
Hikers climbing Mount Pulag must wear thick jackets because temperatures can drop to freezing, causing dangerous hypothermia.
Living near the marshy areas of the Agusan Marsh requires using mosquito nets to prevent dengue from stagnant wetland waters.
Snorkelers in the Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park must avoid touching corals to prevent painful cuts and marine infections.
Families in Benguet province should evacuate immediately during heavy rains because saturated mountain soils easily trigger deadly landslides.
After a strong earthquake, coastal communities facing the West Philippine Sea must immediately walk to higher ground to avoid tsunamis.
Boaters on Laguna de Bay should wear life jackets because sudden strong winds can easily capsize small wooden boats.
Because the Philippines lies near the equator, students in Manila must drink extra water outdoors to prevent severe heatstroke.
Exploring the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River requires wearing hard hats to protect your head from low, rocky cave ceilings.
Drinking untreated water from mountain springs in the Cordillera Administrative Region can cause severe diarrhea from hidden bacteria.
